text: A check stops with a clear answer when GPUs are held by someone else, and a measurement stopped by the scheduler leaves no server behind.
The host-to-GPU copy is measured one GPU at a time; each target says the tokens of its mean request; configurations are compared at the same speed per user.
Power has a stated scope: the serving GPU boards, every board of the node, and the CPU packages or a node meter where they can be read.
The node is checked before a run and watched during it (power limit, clocks, throttling, links, memory errors), and accuracy is scored.
Every p99 carries its 95 % interval and a margin; the server's own counters are read for each window; one run can sweep several latency targets.
A report keeps every priced endpoint, so a page can price it again.
The first measurements: the request rate confirmed within a p99 target for the time to first token and the time per output token, with board power.
